note: Second-generation AR antagonists (enzalutamide, apalutamide, darolutamide) were built on AR-overexpressing LNCaP/AR castrate xenografts; scored for castration-resistant disease, the population they were first prescribed for.
label: Prostate cancer (AR antagonists)

engagement.model: AR-overexpressing LNCaP xenografts in castrate mice
engagement.note: Modest AR overexpression made xenografts castration-resistant and turned bicalutamide into an agonist; the screening model for the class.
engagement.short: AR-high xenografts turn bicalutamide into agonist
engagement.quote: Androgen receptor antagonists showed agonistic activity in cells with increased androgen receptor levels; this antagonist-agonist conversion was associated with alterations in the recruitment of coactivators and corepressors to the promoters of androgen receptor target genes.

engagement.note: LNCaP/AR cells predicted antagonism without agonism; 13 of 30 CRPC patients had sustained >50% PSA falls, the AR-target read-out.
engagement.quote: While preliminary, these clinical data appear promising and validate the persistent role of AR in driving castration-resistant disease.
engagement.judgement: Same paper carries the mouse and the patient data. Scher 2010 (doi 10.1016/S0140-6736(10)60172-9) added direct AR occupancy: FDHT-PET displacement 20-100% in 22 patients, maximal at 150 mg. Joseph 2013 (doi 10.1158/2159-8290.CD-13-0226) later found the model-derived F876L resistance mutation in plasma DNA of ARN-509 progressors; corroborates, no status change.

dose.note: Xenograft regression and AR-reporter suppression tracked dose from 0.1 to 10 mg/kg; mouse trough ~23 µM set the exposure target.
dose.quote: antitumor activity in the LNCaP/AR model is dose-dependent, with some slowing of tumor growth at 0.1 mg/kg RD162 and a few tumor regressions at 1 mg/kg
dose.judgement: The dose-response curve quoted is for RD162, the sibling compound; MDV3100 was dosed in the same model with matching tumour responses and PK.

dose.note: Steady-state serum ~10 µg/mL at 150 mg matched xenograft-effective levels; FDHT-PET AR binding saturated at ~5-15 µg/mL.
dose.quote: Importantly, the steady-state serum concentrations observed in the 150 mg cohort (approximately 10 μg/mL) were comparable to those found to be effective in xenograft models of CRPC.
dose.reason: Patient serum level matched mouse-effective level
dose.judgement: The phase-3 dose (160 mg) sits on the exposure plateau the model implied; the ceiling (240 mg MTD) came from fatigue and seizures, not from the model. For apalutamide, Rathkopf 2013 (doi 10.1200/JCO.2013.50.1684; registry results 2018-07-27) saw FDHT-PET saturation at >=120 mg and chose 240 mg 'based on integration of preclinical and clinical data'; Clegg 2012 (doi 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-11-3948) had put the mouse optimal dose at 30 mg/kg.

efficacy.model: AR-overexpressing LNCaP xenografts in castrate mice
efficacy.note: AR overexpression alone converted LNCaP xenografts from hormone-sensitive to castration-resistant growth; no drug-to-patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: This increase in androgen receptor mRNA and protein was both necessary and sufficient to convert prostate cancer growth from a hormone-sensitive to a hormone-refractory stage, and was dependent on a functional ligand-binding domain.

efficacy.note: Xenografts regressed on MDV3100; in 140 CRPC patients 56% had >=50% PSA falls, 22% soft-tissue responses, radiological TTP 47 weeks.
efficacy.quote: The clinical results reported here establish that MDV3100 has significant antitumor activity in men with chemotherapy-naive and chemotherapy-treated CRPC, thereby validating the preclinical models.
efficacy.judgement: AFFIRM (Scher 2012, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1207506; registry results 2012-10-30) then showed overall survival 18.4 vs 13.6 months at 160 mg; apalutamide (SPARTAN 2018, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1715546) and darolutamide (ARAMIS 2019, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1815671) repeated the pattern in nmCRPC.

efficacy.note: The same xenograft approach foresaw only stable disease and partial agonism for BMS-641988; its phase I closed for limited activity and a seizure.
efficacy.quote: Although the clinical outcomes of predominantly stable disease and partial agonism were similar to what was observed in the preclinical evaluation of the compound
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: BMS-641988's preclinical package used castrate xenografts of the same type as the class, not the LNCaP/AR line itself; the authors themselves state the clinic matched the model's stable-disease/partial-agonism picture before the drug was dropped (abstract-level reading). TERRAIN (Shore 2016, doi 10.1016/S1470-2045(15)00518-5; registry results 2015-12-03) gave a second discriminating case: Tran 2009's model had bicalutamide failing (7/12 tumours progressed) and TERRAIN found PFS 5.8 vs 15.7 months against enzalutamide. Registry: BMS-641988 phase I is NCT00326586 (completed, no results ever posted), so registry_date stays null.

safety.model: Mouse seizure model with GABA-A current assay
safety.note: AR antagonists seized mice via GABA-A off-target; clinic matched: enzalutamide 0.9% seizures, BMS-641988 phase I closed after a seizure.
safety.quote: As a drug class, AR antagonists cause seizure in animals by an off-target mechanism and are found in vitro to inhibit GABA-A currents. Clinical trials of candidate next generation AR antagonists identify seizure as a clinical safety risk.
safety.reason: Mouse seizure signal held in patients
safety.judgement: Model first use and first comparison are the same paper, so there is no untested opener; abstract-level reading (The Prostate is paywalled). The FDA pharmacology review for NDA 203415 (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2012/203415Orig1s000PharmR.pdf) quantifies it: convulsions in mice at >=100 mg/kg/day (0.6x human AUC), GABA-A IC50 2.6 µM, 0.9% patient seizures; the 2012 label reports 7 of 800. The flagged failure is BMS-641988 (Rathkopf 2011, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-10-2955): one seizure at 60 mg contributed to study closure. Darolutamide later ran the prediction the other way: negligible mouse brain penetrance (Moilanen 2015, doi 10.1038/srep12007) and no seizure excess in ARAMIS (Fizazi 2019, doi 10.1056/NEJMoa1815671; registry results 2019-10-29). registry_date is the MDV3100 phase 1-2 trial NCT00510718; the BMS-641988 trial NCT00326586 never posted results.
